questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.

wrongReasons.much: 'much' is used with uncountable nouns like water or money. 'Chairs' is a plural countable noun, so we use 'many'.
wrongReasons.some: 'some' is normally used in positive sentences. This sentence is negative (aren't), so 'some' does not fit.
wrongReasons.little: 'little' is used with uncountable nouns. 'Chairs' is countable.

questions.text: There aren't ___ chairs in the room.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.
questions.explanation: Use 'to' after verbs of movement and 'on' with days of the week.

wrongReasons.0:at: After a verb of movement like 'goes' we use 'to' for the destination, not 'at'.
wrongReasons.0:in: 'in' means inside a place. After 'goes' we use 'to' for the destination.
wrongReasons.0:on: 'on' is used with days and surfaces. For the destination after 'goes' we use 'to'.
wrongReasons.1:at: 'at' is used with exact times (at six o'clock). With days of the week we use 'on'.
wrongReasons.1:in: 'in' is used with months, years and parts of the day (in the morning). With days of the week we use 'on'.
wrongReasons.1:to: 'to' shows direction or destination. With days of the week we use 'on'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the box.
questions.explanation: 'Never' means 0% of the time. It fits with someone who is a vegetarian.

wrongReasons.always: 'always' means 100% of the time. A vegetarian does not eat meat, so this does not make sense.
wrongReasons.sometimes: 'sometimes' means part of the time. A vegetarian never eats meat.

questions.text: I ___ eat meat. I am a vegetarian.
